clue.text: Order to appear Monday featuring in calculations

indicators.note: a thing featuring in another sits within it, so the day's abbreviation goes inside the word for calculations

parts.note: calculations are sums

explanation.surface: A court order demanding someone turn up, dropped into a Monday's accounts.
explanation.definitionFit: A summons is a legal notice commanding a person to attend court.

clue.text: In play, strip out issue having no basis in reality

indicators.note: letters in play are being tossed about and rearranged, so the following words are shuffled

explanation.surface: Someone removing an issue from a stage play, which then seems unfounded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In play' rearranges the thirteen letters of STRIP OUT ISSUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Superstitious beliefs rest on irrational fears and omens rather than evidence.

clue.text: Mike came after Victor's gone with a partner

parts.note: Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: Victor having gone means that letter is taken out of the word for came

parts.note: came means arrived
Victor is V in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Mike turned up once Victor had left, bringing someone along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone' signals that Victor's letter drops out of the word for came.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone married has a spouse, a lifelong partner.

clue.text: Huge quantity of copy, editor annoyed naturally at first

indicators.note: at first asks for the opening letter of each of the five words before it

explanation.surface: An editor naturally gets annoyed by a vast amount of copy to handle.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocean of something is informal for an enormous amount, like oceans of time.

clue.text: Speaks sharply, furious, in quick appraisal

parts.note: to snap is to speak sharply, so speaks sharply is snaps
furious means hot, as in hot under the collar

explanation.surface: Someone snapping angrily when giving a fast assessment.
explanation.definitionFit: A snapshot is a brief overview of a situation at a given moment.

clue.text: One's prepared to welcome returning soldier, well-groomed

indicators.note: welcoming someone takes them in, so the soldier goes inside the rearranged letters
prepared means made up or worked over, so the letters of One's are rearranged
returning means the soldier's letters are read backwards

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: Someone getting ready to greet a soldier coming home, looking smart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges One's into SONE; 'returning' and 'to welcome' put the reversed soldier into its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Soigné is a French borrowing for elegantly dressed and carefully groomed.

clue.text: Sort of pudding divided by Poles in final stage

indicators.note: something divided by another has it running through its middle, so the poles split the pudding word

parts.note: suet pudding is a British steamed dessert, so suet is a sort of pudding
N and S are the North and South Poles

explanation.surface: A pudding split between Polish diners at the end of a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Suet pudding is a heavy British steamed dessert; 'divided by' splits it with the two Poles.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunset is used figuratively for the closing period of something, as in sunset years.

clue.text: Key incoming item needing worker's support

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below, so the worker comes after the import

parts.note: an import is an item brought into a country
an ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A vital imported part that needs a labourer to prop it up.
explanation.definitionFit: Key used as an adjective means crucial or of great significance.

clue.text: Feed sorted out in hours

indicators.note: sorted out means put into a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Feeding arranged within a couple of hours.
explanation.definitionFit: To nourish is to provide food needed for growth and health.

clue.text: Simple housing as alternative to extremely choice in China

indicators.note: housing means holding inside, so the plain word contains the other pieces

parts.note: simple means plain
or introduces an alternative

indicators.note: extremely asks for the outer letters of the word choice

explanation.surface: A modest dwelling as an option to a very select one in China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' at the end looks like the country; it is the fine pottery. 'housing' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: China is the everyday name for porcelain, the fine ceramic first made in that country.

clue.text: Fleshy fruit, pleasing initially

parts.note: a plum is a fruit

indicators.note: initially asks for the first letter of pleasing

explanation.surface: A juicy piece of fruit that looks pleasing at first glance.
explanation.definitionFit: Plump describes a rounded, well-padded body, the same sense as fleshy.

clue.text: Sort of management pattern, heartless, top people in charge?

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of pattern is removed

parts.note: the A-list is the top people, the celebrity elite

explanation.surface: A management style patterned on a cold elite in control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes the central T from PATTERN to leave PATERN.
explanation.definitionFit: Paternalistic management makes decisions for staff, like a father knowing best.

clue.text: With no support at the outset, call time on period in charge

indicators.note: with no means the following letter is dropped from the word for quitting

parts.note: to call time on a job is to resign from it

indicators.note: at the outset asks for the first letter of support

explanation.surface: Losing backing early, a leader ends their time in office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With no' and 'at the outset' remove S, the start of support, from RESIGN.
explanation.definitionFit: A reign is the time a monarch or other ruler holds power.

clue.text: Source of flavour in foreign pantries impressing Monsieur?

indicators.note: impressing means pressing in, so the anagrammed letters hold the abbreviation inside
foreign means strange or altered, so the letters of pantries are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something tasty found in a foreign larder that delights a Frenchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foreign' rearranges PANTRIES and 'impressing' puts M into that mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Spearmint is a mint plant whose oil flavours gum and toothpaste.

clue.text: Odd bet, yearly after vacation, could make 1950s guy

indicators.note: could make says these letters can be reworked into the answer
vacation empties a word, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A strange annual wager, once its centre is cleared, producing a postwar figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after vacation' empties yearly and 'could make' signals the anagram. Teddy boys were 1950s British youths in Edwardian-style drape jackets.
explanation.definitionFit: Teddy boys were a 1950s British youth subculture, so the answer is a guy of that decade.

clue.text: He has many chats at sea?

definitions.text: He has many chats at sea?

indicators.note: at sea means confused or in disarray, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sailor who talks a lot while out on the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges MANY CHATS; the whole clue also describes a sociable sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: A yachtsman sails a yacht, so may well chat a great deal at sea.

clue.text: Article by artist? Right to a certain degree

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Asking whether a piece written by a painter is correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' sets the article beside the artist; the pieces run RA, THE, R.
explanation.definitionFit: Rather means somewhat or fairly, describing a moderate extent.

clue.text: 150 having fun

parts.note: CL is 150 in Roman numerals
having means owning

explanation.surface: A hundred and fifty people enjoying themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Clowning is playful fooling around, a form of fun.

clue.text: Channel showing leading couples in training, English champions

indicators.note: leading couples asks for the first two letters of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A sports channel featuring top pairs in training with English champions.
explanation.walkthrough: The first two letters of training, English and champions give TR, EN, CH.
explanation.definitionFit: A trench is a long narrow ditch, a channel dug in the ground.

clue.text: Setter in conversation with tree? Nonsense

indicators.note: in conversation means spoken, so the word is given by how it sounds

parts.note: the setter refers to themselves as I
the ash is a tree

explanation.surface: A crossword setter chatting to a tree, which is absurd.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter is I, and 'in conversation' turns that into EYE by its sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyewash is informal for talk meant to deceive, which is nonsense or humbug.

clue.text: See where money is held in centre of seafarer ships

indicators.note: in means these pieces go inside the middle letters of seafarer
centre of asks for the middle two letters of seafarer

parts.note: lo is an old word for see, as in lo and behold
a till is the drawer where a shop's money is held

explanation.surface: Pointing out where the cash is kept aboard a sailor's ships.
explanation.definitionFit: A flotilla is a small fleet of ships or boats.

clue.text: Having reversed direction, Berkshire team ahead

indicators.note: swapping one direction for the opposite turns right into left in the team's name

parts.note: Reading FC is the football club of Reading, in the English county of Berkshire

explanation.surface: A football side, after a change of tactics, getting in front.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading is a town in Berkshire, an English county; 'Having reversed direction' replaces R (right) with L (left).
explanation.definitionFit: Leading means in front or first, the same as ahead in a race.

clue.text: Rugged — shout about recycled gag

indicators.note: about means around, so the shout surrounds the reworked joke

parts.note: a shout is a cry

indicators.note: recycled means the letters of gag are processed again into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone shouting about a joke that has been used before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recycled' gives AGG, the rearranged joke, which 'about' places inside the shout.
explanation.definitionFit: Craggy describes rough rocky landscape, or a deeply lined weathered face.

clue.text: Fielder's error and downfall

definitions.meaning: in cricket an ... is a fielder's throw that goes past the stumps, giving away extra runs
the toppling of a ruler or government

explanation.surface: A cricketer's mistake leading to his ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a fielder's wild throw at the stumps that runs away for extra runs is an overthrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Overthrow covers both a cricket misfield and the removal of a regime from power.

clue.text: National misread quip — nothing odd in that

indicators.note: with nothing odd left in the words, only their even letters remain

explanation.surface: A joke misunderstood by a citizen, though nobody found that strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nothing odd in that' drops the odd letters of MISREAD QUIP, keeping I, R, A, Q, I.
explanation.definitionFit: A national is a citizen of a country, here one from Iraq.

clue.text: Insect victim, a goner? Not entirely

indicators.note: not entirely means only part of these words is used, so the answer sits within them

explanation.surface: An insect that falls victim and is done for.
explanation.definitionFit: The imago is the final adult stage of an insect after metamorphosis.

clue.text: Large group from South, cordial

parts.note: cordial means warm and friendly

explanation.surface: A big crowd arriving from the south, all friendly.
explanation.definitionFit: A swarm is a large crowd of insects or people moving together.

clue.text: Unexpected gratuities European left for musician

indicators.note: unexpected means turning out differently, so the letters are rearranged
the European having left means its letter is not part of the mix

explanation.surface: Surprise tips left by a European for a performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' drops the E from GRATUITIES, and 'Unexpected' rearranges what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: A guitarist is a musician who plays the guitar.

clue.text: Call, ultimately dodgy and not genuine

parts.note: to call someone is to phone them

indicators.note: ultimately asks for the final letter of dodgy

explanation.surface: A dubious phone call that turns out to be a scam.
explanation.definitionFit: Phoney means fake or counterfeit, the opposite of authentic.

clue.text: Eg corgi, lively, in this rural poem?

indicators.note: lively means energetic and jumping about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a frisky corgi features in a pastoral verse.
explanation.definitionFit: A georgic is a poem on farming and country life, after Virgil's Georgics.
